issues.failure_explanation: The displayed recursive formula for the coefficient of Δg sums over ℓ and over tuples m_1+...+m_k=i-ℓ, but it never quantifies or sums over k. As written, the coefficient is not well-defined; the proof and the abstract recursion require an additional sum over k=1,...,i-ℓ.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the missing summation over k in the Δg recursion and align the indices with the abstract recursion and proof.
issues.overall_effect: The LTE coefficient recursion is incomplete, so the tree expansion, main LTE theorem, and global convergence proof that depend on it are unsupported as written.
issues.title: LTE Δg recursion missing summation over k
issues.why_classification: This is a local formula correction that preserves the stated LTE structure and all downstream rates once inserted.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: All partial derivatives of $g$ up to order $r$ exist and are continuous, and $y$ is $r+1$ times continuously differentiable.

issues.failure_explanation: To obtain an O(h^{r+1}) remainder after summing through order r, the proof bounds the difference of the r-th derivative by D'h. That requires the r-th derivative to be Lipschitz or, equivalently, (r+1)-differentiability. The assumptions only provide r continuous derivatives of g and r+1 derivatives of the exact solution, so the needed bound is unestablished.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Strengthen the regularity assumption (e.g., derivatives of g up to r+1) or prove the required Lipschitz property for the r-th derivative, and adjust the r hypotheses in dependent convergence results.
issues.overall_effect: The stated remainder estimates in the LTE lemma, and the global error rates that rely on them, lack a supported regularity argument.
issues.title: LTE Taylor remainder assumes one more derivative than provided
issues.why_classification: The repair is contained but changes the regularity hypothesis or adds a nontrivial differentiability argument; the main rates survive under the strengthened condition.

issues.failure_explanation: The recurrence defines v_{i+1} with the linear term α_i, but the induction step substitutes α_{i+1}. Consequently the bushy-tree term added in the induction is indexed incorrectly and the proof does not establish the stated recursion.

failure_location.quote: The term $\ac[i+1]$ in \cref{eq:sum2} then adds the missing lone tree to the sum

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Correct α_{i+1} to α_i in the induction step and align the bushy tree index accordingly.
issues.overall_effect: The abstract tree recursion lemma, used to derive the LTE tree representation and the main order-condition theorem, has an invalid induction step as written.
issues.title: Abstract recursion proof uses wrong α index
issues.why_classification: The fix is a local off-by-one correction to the proof; the lemma statement and downstream results are preserved.

issues.failure_explanation: The final-error tree coefficients are Δy[1][i], not Δy[0][i]. The proof sets v_i=Δy[0][i] and uses α_i built from γ_i and γhat_i, which matches a recurrence for v_i, whereas the abstract lemma applies to v_{i+1}=α_i. As written, the application to the ψ expansion is mismatched.

failure_location.quote: Similarly, the result for $\varphi(\treevar)= \oc[\treevar][Z][\timevar]$ follows by setting $\mathbb{V} = \R^{\nvar}$, $\dy[0][i] = \vy[i]$

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Reindex the ψ application to the abstract recursion (for example, set v_i to the coefficient of order i+1 or adjust the abstract recurrence) so that α_i matches Δy[1][i+1].
issues.overall_effect: The proof of the tree representation for the one-step error Δy[1] is unsupported, affecting the main LTE vanishing result and the global convergence theorem.
issues.title: Tree theorem ψ-application uses wrong or undefined index
issues.why_classification: This is a local proof reindexing; the theorem statement and intended tree recursion remain intact.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: For any set of vectors $\beta_j \in \R^s, u_j \in \R^{\nvar}$ ($j = 1, \ldots, k$), the following holds:

issues.failure_explanation: The left-hand side applies G to k vectors β_j⊗u_j, but the right-hand side uses the product β_1×...×β_s. For k≠s this is either undefined (if s>k) or includes extra factors (if k>s). The identity requires β_1×...×β_k.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace β_s by β_k in the right-hand side of Eq:KroneckerIdentity.
issues.overall_effect: The Kronecker identity is a premise for the vector-space representation lemma and for extracting the coefficient orthogonality in the main LTE theorem; as written it is false.
issues.title: Kronecker identity multiplies β_1 through β_s instead of β_k
issues.why_classification: The correction is a single forced index change; the subsequent inferences remain valid once the identity is correct.

issues.failure_explanation: The theorem's 'In particular' estimate is written for Δy[0], the initial error, but the preceding vanishing result and the tree series are for the one-step error Δy[1]. The proof therefore establishes a different bound than the displayed statement.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Change Δy[0] in Eq:LTE_ErrorEst to Δy[1] (or the corresponding one-step error variable).
issues.overall_effect: The main local error estimate is misstated; the global convergence theorem uses the intended one-step LTE bound, not the literal Δy[0] statement.
issues.title: Main LTE theorem bounds Δy[0] instead of Δy[1]
issues.why_classification: A one-symbol index correction restores the intended statement without changing the mathematical content.

issues.failure_explanation: The displayed 5g condition has the form b^T A^{j} C A^{m}(c^2/2-Ac), which is implied by the 4b condition (with Cayley-Hamilton reduction of the leading power). Condition 3a instead involves b^T A^{j}(c^3/6-Ac^2/2) and does not generally imply 5g.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Correct the 'Implied By' entry for 5g to 4b or provide a valid derivation from the lower-order conditions actually implied.
issues.overall_effect: The table's stated redundancy for 5g is false, although the condition itself is still listed among the semilinear order conditions.
issues.title: Order condition 5g is not implied by 3a
issues.why_classification: Only the explanatory implication column is affected; the order condition set and main theory do not change.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Here AS- and ASI-stability ensure the existence and boundedness of the matrix inverses and $R(Z)$.

issues.failure_explanation: The paper defines only the scalar stability function R(z). The C-stability lemma uses R(Z) as an N×N operator, but no matrix extension or one-step linear propagator R(Z) is defined. The proof therefore relies on an undefined object.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Define R(Z) as the linear one-step propagator (for example via the Cayley-Hamilton polynomial in Z corresponding to the scalar R(z)) before the lemma and use that definition in the proof.
issues.overall_effect: The C-stability lemma and the global error recurrence that uses it are ill-defined until R(Z) is specified.
issues.title: Matrix R(Z) used in C-stability lemma is undefined
issues.why_classification: The missing definition is a local notational/constructive gap; once R(Z) is defined, the lemma statement is the intended one.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: by \cref{Eq:Rcondition}, the rational function $(1 - R(z))^{-1}$ has a single simple pole at $z=0$ on $\C^{-}$;

issues.failure_explanation: The assumptions allow J, and hence Z=hJ, to be singular. If Z has a zero eigenvalue, then R(0)=1 and I-R(Z) is not invertible, so the displayed ξ_{n-1} is undefined. The later observation that the scalar pole at z=0 is removable does not replace the undefined matrix inverse with a bounded extension in the proof.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Either assume I-R(Z) is invertible for the relevant Z or redefine ξ using the bounded removable extension of the rational function and verify the estimates with that extension.
issues.overall_effect: The superconvergence part of the global error theorem is unsupported for semilinear problems with zero eigenvalues in the stiff linear part.
issues.title: Superconvergence proof divides by I-R(Z) without handling singular Z
issues.why_classification: The theorem can likely be salvaged by a contained proof repair using the removable pole, but as written the central superconvergence guarantee has an unhandled degenerate regime.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: The ten-stage ESDIRK-(10,5,4) method is fifth-order accurate with a semilinear order of four.
Using the simplest step-number sequence of ${1, 2}$ for the extrapolation results in a 19 stage method.

issues.failure_explanation: The table attributes properties to EDIRK-(19,5,4) by citing app:ESDIRK-(1054), which actually contains the ESDIRK-(10,5,4) coefficients. The source does not provide coefficients for EDIRK-(19,5,4), and the described Richardson extrapolation from EDIRK-(7,4,4) is not sufficiently explicit to define the 19-stage method or verify the tabulated stability and error constants.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Provide explicit coefficients or a complete algorithmic construction for EDIRK-(19,5,4), or correct the table to refer to the actually provided EDIRK-(7,4,4) method and its appendix.
issues.overall_effect: One advertised method, EDIRK-(19,5,4), and its tabulated guarantees are not established by the source.
issues.title: EDIRK-(19,5,4) method not fully specified and table cites wrong appendix
issues.why_classification: The repair is local to one secondary method, but the source currently lacks a supported definition of that method and its stated properties.
